research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10376 at 17 FR 6681 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed July 18, 1952; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the July 22, 1952 issue. The register title is Providing for Permanent Appointments in the Field Service of the Post Office Department.  Inventory corrected: one clause, offsets 751 to 3651 of the held text, from the enacting words through section 3. The dossier's clause span (offsets 3054 to 3570) covers only paragraph 2(b) of the order, not the whole order. Content: section 1 provides that, notwithstanding section 1(a) of Executive Order No. 10180 of November 13, 1950 and to the extent authorized by law, appointments to field-service positions of the Post Office Department whose salary rates are fixed by the act of July 6, 1945 are to be made on a permanent basis; section 2(a) converts, under conditions the Civil Service Commission prescribes, indefinite appointments of certain such employees to probational or permanent appointments as of the effective date, limited by the number of vacancies in the authorized complement; section 2(b) does the same for employees reemployed after armed-forces service on application within ninety days after honorable discharge (or after hospitalization continuing not more than one year); section 3 makes the order effective thirty days after its date. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10376 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry, extracted separately and matched by position, reads providing for permanent appointments in the field service of the Post Office Department). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Earlier-end check: no fixed end date or termination clause appears in the order; section 3 sets only an effective date (thirty days after July 18, 1952). Executive Order 10180 is cited by this order and is earlier, so it is not a later event. The packet's number search finds no held text citing this order, and the dossier chain names only Executive Order 12553. No held source shows whether the section 2 conversions were completed or whether a statute or regulation displaced section 1 before 1986, so no earlier end is claimed. Prior research: the dossier shows no canonical prior claim and no conflicting versions. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning.
